gaps.sentence: The company ___ interest on the money it borrows.
gaps.explanation: pay interest is the standard financial collocation.

gaps.sentence: Her talk really ___ home the urgency of the situation.
gaps.explanation: 'Drive something home' = make it fully understood.

gaps.sentence: She was bitterly ___ when her proposal was rejected.
gaps.hint: adjective collocating with 'bitterly' after bad news
gaps.explanation: bitterly disappointed is the standard collocation; 'bitterly' combines with negative feelings.

gaps.sentence: I'd like to ___ a suggestion, if I may.
gaps.explanation: make a suggestion is the fixed collocation; 'say a suggestion' is not used.

gaps.sentence: The crash left several passengers seriously ___.
gaps.explanation: seriously injured is the standard collocation describing bad injuries in accidents.

gaps.sentence: The manager ___ an announcement about the changes yesterday.
gaps.explanation: make an announcement is the fixed collocation for stating something publicly.

gaps.sentence: Stop ___ money on things you never use.
gaps.hint: to use money on useless things; -ing form after 'Stop'
gaps.explanation: waste money on something means to spend it on useless things; 'stop' is followed by the -ing form.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.
